instructions: Drain and rinse the chickpeas. Juice the lemons. That should be about 1/3 cup.
Put the chickpeas in a food processor with the tahini, garlic, lemon juice and 3/4 tsp of the salt. Blend for 2 minutes, scraping down the sides once.
With the processor running, add cold water 1 tbsp at a time, up to 4 tbsp, until it's smooth and creamy.
Spread the blended chickpeas in a shallow wide bowl, then press a shallow well into the center with the back of a spoon.
Finely dice the onion. Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the onion for 4 minutes, until soft and golden at the edges. Don't rush it.

Add the beef and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt. Leave it alone for 1 minute so it browns, then break it up and cook for 5 minutes, until the moisture has cooked off. You're cooking it to 160°F, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? It's done when there's no pink left.
Stir in the seven spice, paprika and pepper and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant. Take the pan off the heat.
Spoon the beef into the well in the chickpeas. Drizzle the remaining 2 tbsp oil over the chickpeas and scatter 1/4 cup chopped parsley over the top.
Warm the pitas in a dry skillet for 20 seconds per side. Serve with the warm pita.
method_notes: Every version has chickpea hummus with lemon, tahini and garlic, topped with beef browned with Lebanese seven spice. Simply Lebanese (5 from 5 ratings) is the lead for the hummus ratios and the spice step; Cookin' With Mima adds the onion and paprika and the hummus-well plating. Both lists use pine nuts and both are left out to keep the dish nut-free. Lemon is 1/3 cup for two cans, between the two sources. Leftover hummus and beef keep separately in the fridge for 3 days; reheat the beef in a skillet.
